target_customer: Developers building AI applications that need to understand video
problem: Turning video into structured, searchable context for AI requires heavy infrastructure work.

founders.name: Amy Xiao
education: University of Toronto, math and physics
founders.background_notes: From YC page, which lists her in ML and infrastructure roles.

competitors.name: Twelve Labs
competitors.what: Video understanding models and APIs for search and classification
competitors.funding_then: $50M Series A in June 2024 per coverage; earlier $17M seed

technical_complexity.rationale: Orchestrating multimodal models for speech, vision and structured extraction at scale is real infrastructure work built on existing models.

defensibility.rationale: A funded specialist (Twelve Labs) and big cloud vendors offer video understanding; the context layer wedge is thin.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Twelve Labs raised $50M in June 2024; no acquisition of Cloudglue found.

market_need_then: LLM and multimodal models made video analysis feasible in 2024; no sourced demand metrics for Cloudglue were found.

identity.logo: A cloud emoji precedes the name in profiles; no official logo description

brand_strength.rationale: Plain compound name with little sourced brand activity.

outcome_analysis: Cloudglue is active, a small team of four with a video API and the Tinycloud agent in beta. No verified funding or traction is public, and a well funded competitor, Twelve Labs, was raising large rounds in 2024, so the outcome is unclear.
notes: PitchBook snippet says $500K raised and a profile says last stage seed; one aggregator only, so unverified and not recorded (PitchBook page returned 403). Matt Pua appears as co-founder on Product Hunt only, not on the YC page, so not listed. Founder education and employers come from the YC page. Outcome search found nothing on the company. Competitor source URL is a Twelve Labs blog about its earlier seed; the Series A date comes from search snippets of 2024 coverage.
